items.q: There were such names as Shorty, Twisted-Mouth George, the Sheik, Slim Willy and Fats Rolland. They and the girls they danced with were our real supporters

ctx.x: We were also playing the two-hour dinner break for the musicians at the Savoy on Sundays. The Savoy only had matinees on Sundays and holidays.

I met a fellow about my age named Bob Sawyer who became a good friend of mine. The first new friend I had made in New York. The dancers that were regular customers and top "Lindy Hoppers" became our friends also. There were such names as Shorty, Twisted-Mouth George, the Sheik, Slim Willy and Fats Rolland. They and the girls they danced with were our real supporters but Bob became a real friend of mine. He showed me how to tie a bow tie. I bought them already tied before that. Now and then, musicians would drop by the Capitol to listen to the band and some would sit in for some jam sessions. One that I had not heard about was a trumpeter named Cuban Bennett. This man was a musician's musician because he had a style in the order of Joe Smith but he did more changes, as harmony was called, and he did not use a plunger like Joe Smith did.
